title: Goods 22 - HGV Speed Limits, Speed Limiters and Truck Licences
source: S.I. No. 75 of 2012 (HGV speed limits); Directive 2002/85/EC (speed limiters); Directive 2006/126/EC and RSA guidance (licence categories and ages)

questions.q: What is the speed limit for a goods vehicle over 3,500 kg on an Irish motorway?
questions.exp:
Goods vehicles with a design gross weight over 3,500 kg: 90 km/h on motorways (raised from 80 km/h in 2012) and 80 km/h on other roads, unless a lower limit applies.
📍 S.I. No. 75 of 2012

questions.q: What is the speed limit for a goods vehicle over 3,500 kg on a national road (not a motorway)?
questions.exp:
On roads other than motorways the ordinary limit for HGVs is 80 km/h, unless the road has a lower limit (for example 50 km/h in towns).
📍 Road traffic speed limits for HGVs

questions.q: At what speed must the speed limiter of a goods vehicle over 3,500 kg be set?
questions.exp:
Goods vehicles over 3,500 kg must have a speed limiter set so the vehicle cannot exceed 90 km/h. Buses and coaches are set at 100 km/h.
📍 Directive 2002/85/EC

questions.q: Who enforces speed limits and speed limiter rules on Irish roads?
questions.exp:
Enforcement of the speed regulations on the road is a matter for the Garda Síochána; the RSA also checks limiters at CVRT and roadside checks.
📍 Dáil answers on HGV speed limits

questions.q: A truck with a speed limiter set at 90 km/h is driving on a national road with an 80 km/h limit. What may it do?
options: Drive at 90 km/h because that is the limiter setting
Drive at no more than 80 km/h
questions.exp:
The limiter is a maximum the vehicle can physically reach; the legal limit on that road is still 80 km/h for HGVs.
📍 HGV speed limits

questions.q: Which licence category covers goods vehicles between 3,500 kg and 7,500 kg?
questions.exp:
C1: vehicles over 3,500 kg and not over 7,500 kg. C: vehicles over 3,500 kg with no upper limit. B is up to 3,500 kg.
📍 Directive 2006/126/EC; RSA licence categories

questions.q: Which licence category is needed to drive an articulated lorry (tractor unit and semi-trailer)?
questions.exp:
A category C vehicle towing a trailer over 750 kg, which includes articulated vehicles and drawbar combinations, needs CE.
📍 Directive 2006/126/EC; RSA licence categories

questions.q: What is the normal minimum age for a category C (truck) licence in Ireland?
questions.exp:
21 for categories C and CE. It drops to 18 for a driver who holds the Driver CPC.
📍 RSA; Dáil answer 14 May 2024

questions.q: A driver who holds the Driver CPC can get a category C licence from the age of:
questions.exp:
The minimum age of 21 for C and CE is lowered to 18 when the driver holds the Driver Certificate of Professional Competence.
📍 Dáil answer 14 May 2024

questions.q: What is the minimum age for a category C1 (small truck) learner permit?
questions.exp:
C1 (3,500 to 7,500 kg): from 18. A full category B licence is needed first.
📍 RSA, truck categories

questions.q: Before applying for a category C learner permit, a driver must hold:
questions.exp:
To learn to drive a truck you must already hold a full category B (car) licence.
📍 RSA, truck categories

questions.q: A haulier's goods vehicle with a design gross weight of 3,500 kg or less (a van) on the motorway follows:
options: The ordinary limits for the road
questions.exp:
The 90/80 km/h HGV limits apply to goods vehicles over 3,500 kg design gross weight. Vans up to 3,500 kg follow the ordinary limits for the road.
📍 HGV speed limits

questions.q: How many hours of periodic training must a truck driver complete every 5 years to keep the Driver CPC?
questions.exp:
35 hours every 5 years (normally one 7-hour module a year) at an RSA-approved centre. The same 35 hours count for both C and D licences.
📍 RSA, Driver CPC

questions.q: Where can a truck driver show proof of the Driver CPC at a roadside check?
questions.exp:
Drivers carry their Driver Qualification Card (DQC) or have the Union code 95 on their driving licence.
📍 RSA, Driver CPC
